key_insight: Using intermediate projected-gradient-descent iterates as training data can substantially increase learning data without extra solver runs, and the paper quantifies this benefit with a Rademacher-complexity generalization bound.
engineering_relevance: This can make data-driven initialization for expensive parametric optimization more efficient, improving closed-loop DDDAS workflows and reducing solve time in engineering design and control pipelines.
method: Augment converged-solution datasets with k-neighborhood solver iterates.
Derive a generalization bound for learning from these iterates using Rademacher complexity.
Demonstrate the projected gradient descent behavior on two one-sided box-constrained quadratic program examples.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical generalization analysis plus two illustrative solver examples, rather than large-scale empirical benchmarking.
watch_item: The approach is developed for one-sided box-constrained quadratic programs and projected gradient descent, so performance and the bound’s usefulness may not transfer directly to other solvers or constraint types.
paper_title: Complexity Bounds and Approaches to Learning Projected Gradient Descent Solver Iterates
